skill.name: freshservice-automation
skill.description: Automate Freshservice ITSM work through Rube MCP, including ticket lookup, ticket creation, bulk updates, service requests, and outbound email tickets.
skill.summary: Automates Freshservice tickets, service requests, and outbound email workflows through Rube MCP.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around MCP tool names and Freshservice parameters, not shell execution. The skill does introduce a real external MCP endpoint and write-capable Freshservice workflows. No evidence found of prompt injection text in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Write-capable workflows lack an explicit approval gate.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before creating tickets, bulk updating tickets, sending outbound email tickets, or creating service requests.

remediation.issue: The external MCP trust boundary is only briefly documented.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users that Rube MCP is a third-party endpoint and advise them to review Freshservice permissions before connecting.

remediation.issue: Outbound email ticket creation can contact requesters or copy recipients.
remediation.suggestion: Require recipient, sender configuration, subject, and body review before invoking outbound email ticket creation.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Freshservice connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `freshservice`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
1. `FRESHSERVICE_LIST_TICKETS` - List tickets with optional filtering and pagination [Required]
2. `FRESHSERVICE_GET_TICKET` - Get detailed information for a specific ticket [Optional]
- `updated_since`: ISO 8601 timestamp to get tickets updated after this time
- Each `include` value consumes additional API credits
- `email`: Requester's email address (provide either email or requester_id)
- Either `email` or `requester_id` must be provided to identify the requester
- `ids`: Array of ticket IDs to update (required)
- `email_config_id`: Email configuration ID for the sender address
- `email_config_id` determines which email address the notification appears to come from
1. `FRESHSERVICE_CREATE_SERVICE_REQUEST` - Create a service request for a catalog item [Required]
- `item_display_id`: Display ID of the catalog item (required)
- `custom_fields`: Custom field values for the service item form
- `parent_ticket_id`: Display ID of a parent ticket (for child requests)
- `item_display_id` can be found in Admin > Service Catalog > item URL (e.g., /service_catalog/items
- Each `include` option consumes additional API credits
- Response data may be nested under `data` or `data.data`
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Ticket IDs can be the internal ID or the display_id shown in the UI
- `email_config_id`: Email configuration ID for the sender address

semantic_findings.title: Write-Capable ITSM Actions Lack Approval Gate
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents ticket creation, bulk ticket updates, outbound email ticket creation, and service request creation without requiring explicit user confirmation before write actions. In an agent workflow, ambiguous instructions could cause unauthorized Freshservice changes or emails.

content.value_statement: Freshservice work can require repeated ticket lookups, updates, and service request steps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through those workflows using Rube MCP.
actual_capabilities: Lists Freshservice tickets with filters, sorting, pagination, and optional include fields.
Gets detailed ticket information when a ticket ID or display ID is available.
Creates incident or request tickets with status, priority, requester, and HTML description fields.
Bulk updates selected tickets with shared update fields through Freshservice tooling.
Creates outbound email tickets and service catalog requests through Rube MCP.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP and an active Freshservice connection before any workflow can run.
Depends on current Freshservice tool schemas returned by Rube MCP.
Does not validate organization-specific custom fields, approvals, or permission rules.
Write actions can change Freshservice records and should be confirmed before execution.

use_cases.title: Review active support queues
use_cases.description: List recent tickets, inspect details, and summarize priorities for a service desk shift.

use_cases.title: Apply consistent ticket updates
use_cases.description: Find related tickets and apply the same status, priority, group, or tag update.

use_cases.title: Submit service catalog requests
use_cases.description: Create service requests with item IDs, requester email, quantity, and custom field values.

prompt_templates.title: List recent tickets
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Freshservice to list open tickets updated since [date]. Show ticket ID, requester, status, priority, and a short summary.

prompt_templates.title: Create an incident ticket
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Freshservice incident for [requester email]. Use subject [subject], priority [priority code], status [status code], and this description: [description].

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a bulk update
prompt_templates.prompt: Find tickets matching [criteria], list the candidate IDs, and wait for my confirmation before applying [shared update fields].

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate service request intake
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a service request for catalog item [item display ID] for [requester email] with quantity [number] and these custom fields: [fields].

output_examples.input: Show high priority open tickets updated this week.
output: Returns a concise ticket list with IDs, subjects, requesters, status, priority, and updated time.
Highlights tickets that need immediate follow-up based on priority and age.

output_examples.input: Create a laptop access service request for a new employee.
output_examples.output: Creates a service request using the catalog item ID, requester email, quantity, and required custom fields after the needed details are provided.

output_examples.input: Close these resolved incident tickets after I approve the list.
output_examples.output: Prepares the selected ticket IDs and shared update fields, then waits for approval before performing the bulk update.

best_practices: Call the tool search first so current Freshservice schemas are used.
Confirm ticket IDs, requester emails, and write actions before changing Freshservice records.
Use pagination and date filters to keep ticket searches focused and reliable.
anti_patterns: Do not bulk update tickets from a broad search without reviewing the selected IDs.
Do not assume status and priority names work when Freshservice expects numeric codes.
Do not send outbound email tickets without reviewing recipients, sender configuration, and message body.

faq.question: What Freshservice tasks can this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps list tickets, get ticket details, create tickets, bulk update tickets, send outbound email tickets, and create service requests.

faq.question: Does it need a Freshservice connection?
faq.answer: Yes. Rube MCP must be available, and the Freshservice connection must show an active status.

faq.question: Can it update many tickets at once?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide bulk updates when you provide selected ticket IDs and shared update fields.

faq.question: Can it create service catalog requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports service requests when you provide the catalog item display ID and required field values.

faq.question: Why should I search tools first?
faq.answer: Freshservice tool schemas can change. Searching first helps the agent use current parameters and avoid stale assumptions.

faq.question: What should I review before write actions?
faq.answer: Review requester details, ticket IDs, status codes, priority codes, recipients, and custom fields before execution.
